title: Assessment of Nutritional Status of Individuals and Families

headings.title: Introduction and Objectives of Nutritional Assessment
headings.content: Nutritional assessment is a systematic process used to determine the nutritional status of individuals and families. By combining multiple evaluation methods, health workers detect early deviations from normal health before overt clinical symptoms manifest. In primary health care settings across Nigeria, routine screening helps identify hidden hunger, protein-energy malnutrition, and overnutrition. The primary goals include establishing baseline data, identifying specific nutrient deficiencies, and monitoring the effectiveness of community health interventions over time.

headings.title: Anthropometric Measurements across the Lifespan
headings.content:
Anthropometry involves the physical measurement of body size, weight, and proportions. These metrics vary significantly depending on age and physiological state.

- **Weight**: Reflects body mass changes; measured using a properly calibrated infant scale or standing scale.
- **Height/Length**: Essential for linear growth tracking; recumbent length is taken for children under two years, while standing height is used for older individuals.
- **Mid-Upper Arm Circumference (MUAC)**: A rapid screening tool for acute malnutrition, particularly useful in field settings using color-coded tapes.
- **Body Mass Index (BMI)**: Calculated as weight in kilograms divided by height in meters squared, categorizing adults into underweight, normal, overweight, or obese ranges.

headings.title: Clinical Examination for Physical Signs of Malnutrition
headings.content:
A targeted physical examination reveals outward signs of vitamin, mineral, and protein deficiencies. Nurses inspect tissues with rapid cell turnover, such as the skin, hair, eyes, and oral cavity, because these areas reflect nutritional stress earliest.

| Body Area | Clinical Sign | Potential Deficiency |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Hair | Sparse, depigmented, easily plucked | Protein-energy malnutrition |
| Eyes | Bitot's spots, corneal xerosis | Vitamin A deficiency |
| Mouth | Angular stomatitis, glossitis | B-complex vitamins (Riboflavin) |
| Skin | Follicular hyperkeratosis, dry scaly skin | Vitamin A or Essential Fatty Acids |

headings.title: Dietary Assessment Methods and Family Food Security
headings.content:
Evaluating what an individual or family eats provides context for anthropometric and clinical findings. Dietary assessment methods range from 24-hour dietary recalls, where a client lists all foods consumed the previous day, to food frequency questionnaires that track habitual intake over weeks or months. 

Beyond individual intake, nurses must assess household food security—the reliable availability and economic access to safe, nutritious food. Poverty, inflation, seasonal crop failures, and poor storage facilities frequently compromise family dietary diversity in rural and peri-urban Nigerian communities. A household that relies on a single staple carbohydrate without adequate proteins and micronutrients remains at high risk for hidden hunger.

headings.title: Biochemical and Laboratory Indicators
headings.content: Laboratory investigations offer objective data to confirm nutritional deficiencies before physical symptoms become severe. Hemoglobin and packed cell volume tests are routinely performed to detect anemia, which is frequently caused by iron deficiency, malaria, or parasitic infestations. Serum albumin levels help evaluate visceral protein status, although inflammation can distort these readings. Urine and stool analyses also reveal underlying infections, such as hookworm, that impair nutrient absorption in the gastrointestinal tract.

headings.title: Vulnerable Groups in Family and Community Nutrition
headings.content: Certain physiological stages and social dynamics increase the risk of malnutrition within families. Pregnant and lactating women have heightened nutritional requirements to support fetal development and milk production. Infants and young children face rapid growth phases combined with immature immune systems, making them exceptionally vulnerable during the weaning period. Furthermore, elderly family members may experience reduced appetite, dental loss, and social isolation, which threaten their nutritional stability.

headings.title: Nursing Interventions and Nutritional Counseling
headings.content: Nutritional assessment data guides the formulation of targeted nursing care plans. Nurses collaborate with dietitians, community health extension workers, and agricultural extension agents to improve community health. Effective nutritional counseling respects local cultural food practices while promoting affordable dietary diversification, exclusive breastfeeding for the first six months of life, and appropriate complementary feeding. When severe acute malnutrition is identified, prompt referral to an outpatient or inpatient therapeutic feeding program is lifesaving.
